overview: Constitutional authorities (CAG, ECI, UPSC, NCSC), the judiciary, Panchayati Raj and governance: 30 official questions (2010-2024). Authorities (11) and judiciary (11) lead; 2023-24 brought 9 statement-based items on powers and safeguards, while 2010-2019 favoured current-affairs one-liners (incumbent CJI, landmark 2016 judgments, first e-court, VVPAT). Public policy as such is not yet asked.

possibility.angle: Constitutional and statutory authorities (CAG, ECI, UPSC, NCSC, delimitation)
possibility.what_they_ask: to whom reports go; removal procedure; powers in investigation; what UPSC is not consulted on; ECI powers and history; firsts (VVPAT); delimitation scope

possibility.angle: Judiciary: Supreme Court and High Courts
possibility.what_they_ask: original jurisdiction scope; independence safeguards; Art. 142 cases; landmark 2016 judgments; incumbents and firsts; judicial academy location

possibility.angle: Panchayati Raj and urban local bodies
possibility.what_they_ask: what article 243G covers; 11th vs 12th Schedule items; AP introduction year/CM; own-revenue of tiers
natural targets: policy cycle stages, NITI Aayog (2015) vs Planning Commission, role of committees and think-tanks, social audit
first model e-court (Gujarat HC, 2009); FCRA cancellation ground; PMLA powers and Schedule

traps.trap: [Report recipient] Report sent to the PM instead of the President
traps.spot: Options 'Prime Minister' / 'Parliament' for a constitutional body's report
traps.fix: CAG (Union), NCSC, NCST, UPSC, FC report to the President; State bodies and CAG (State) to the Governor
traps.pyq: CAG Union report → The President [group1-prelims-2010#89]; NCSC 'report to the Prime Minister' is not a function [group1-prelims-2023-paper1#50]

traps.trap: Power to recommend inflated to power to dismiss
traps.spot: 'ECI can order the Government to dismiss officials'
traps.fix: ECI can seek transfer, suspension or disciplinary action; officials are deemed on deputation, not dismissed by it
traps.pyq: Statement II false → 'I and III only' [group1-prelims-2023-paper1#36]

traps.spot: 'Judges removed by the CJI'; 'CAG not removed like an SC judge'
traps.fix: SC judges and the CAG are removed by the President after a special-majority address of both Houses
traps.pyq: Statement II false [group1-prelims-2023-paper1#37]; CAG statement I false [group1-prelims-2024-paper1#34]

traps.trap: Non-federal dispute put into original jurisdiction
traps.spot: Art. 131 lists including election disputes or Centre-UT disputes
traps.fix: Art. 131 = Centre-State and inter-State disputes only; Parliament/Assembly election petitions go to High Courts
traps.pyq: 'II and III' are not original jurisdiction [group1-prelims-2023-paper1#38]

traps.trap: Urban subject placed in the rural schedule
traps.fix: Slum improvement and upgradation is in the 12th Schedule; women and child, PDS, libraries, markets are 11th
traps.pyq: Item IV excluded → 'I, II, III and V' [group1-prelims-2023-paper1#52]

traps.trap: Exception to a consultation rule removed
traps.fix: Art. 320(4): UPSC is not consulted on reservation of posts
traps.pyq: 'Manner of reservation' is not a function [group1-prelims-2023-paper1#51]

traps.trap: Case swapped with another landmark of the same year
traps.spot: Four 2016-18 case names for one subject
traps.fix: Swaraj Abhiyan = drought; PUCL = right to food; Common Cause = living will; K. Balu = highway liquor ban (Art. 142)
traps.pyq: Drought guidelines → Swaraj Abhiyan [group1-prelims-2017-paper1#1]; Art. 142 → highway liquor ban [group1-prelims-2017-paper1#150]

techniques.name: Recipient table
techniques.how: [Who gets the report] Keep one table: President-bound vs Governor-bound reports; any other recipient in an option is wrong.
techniques.example: NCSC reports to the President under Art. 338(5) → the PM option is the non-function [group1-prelims-2023-paper1#50]

techniques.name: Recommend vs order test
techniques.how: For any commission's power, ask: can it order, or only recommend/summon? Most bodies have civil-court powers of inquiry but no power to dismiss.
techniques.example: NCSC: affidavits, records, summons all are Art. 338(8) civil-court powers → 'All of the above' [group1-prelims-2023-paper1#39]

techniques.name: Date-of-exam incumbent fix
techniques.how: For 'present' or 'recent' questions, fix the exam date and drop predecessors and successors.
techniques.example: Exam Sept 2010 → S.H. Kapadia (from May 2010), not K.G. Balakrishnan [group1-prelims-2010#93]

techniques.name: Tenure-to-event mapping
techniques.how: Map an event year to the CM/PM/CJI of that year by tenure ranges.
techniques.example: Panchayati Raj in AP 1959 → N. Sanjeeva Reddy (1956-60); Sanjeevaiah took over in 1960 [group1-prelims-2010-reexam#15]

techniques.name: Firsts chain
techniques.how: For technology firsts keep three steps: first trial, first full State, all-India.
techniques.example: VVPAT: Noksen bypoll 2013 → Goa 2017 → all LS seats 2019 → 'By poll in Nagaland, 2013' [group1-prelims-2017-paper1#145]

techniques.name: Part IX article ladder
techniques.how: 243B tiers, 243C composition, 243D reservation, 243E term, 243G powers, 243H taxes, 243-I SFC, 243K SEC.
techniques.example: 243G → powers and functions of Panchayats; finance options are 243H [group1-prelims-2010#72]

anchors: Art. 148 CAG removed like an SC judge; Art. 151 reports to President / Governor
Art. 324 ECI; multi-member since 1993; officials on election duty deemed on deputation
Art. 320(4): UPSC not consulted on reservation
Art. 338(5), 338(8): NCSC reports to President; civil-court powers
Art. 131 original jurisdiction = federal disputes; election petitions to High Courts
Art. 124(4) judges removed by President after special-majority address
Panchayati Raj in AP from 1 November 1959 (N. Sanjeeva Reddy)
First model e-court: Gujarat HC, Ahmedabad, 8 Feb 2009
PMLA 2002 in force 2005; ED can attach proceeds of crime
checklist: Who receives the report, who removes the officer? Recall the article.
Order, recommend or inquire? Most bodies cannot order dismissal.
'Present' or 'recent': fix the exam date first.
Case-name options: tie each case to its one subject.
